healthcareSystem: French overseas territory with a French-standard healthcare system. Centre Hospitalier de la Polynésie Française (CHPF) in Tahiti is modern and well-equipped. Outer islands have dispensaries with limited capabilities. French social security system applies to residents; tourists pay out of pocket.
qualityNotes: Healthcare in Tahiti is good by Pacific Island standards with modern facilities at CHPF. Bora Bora and Moorea have medical centers for routine care. Remote atolls have basic dispensaries only. For very complex cases, patients are evacuated to metropolitan France, New Zealand, or Australia.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Papeete open 7:30am-6pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. A duty pharmacy system operates for after-hours needs. Outer islands have limited pharmacy access — major resorts may have basic supplies.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Tahiti are well-stocked and follow French pharmaceutical standards. Pharmacists speak French; some speak English in tourist areas. Medications may use French brand names. Bring essential medications — outer islands have very limited supplies. Look for the green cross (croix verte) pharmacy sign.
prescriptionRules: French prescription rules apply. Antibiotics and many medications require a prescription (ordonnance). Pharmacists can advise and sell appropriate OTC medications. French medical standards are followed.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal under French law. Strict enforcement.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled under French regulations. Carry a doctor's prescription, ideally in French, and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. French regulations may differ from your home country — check before travel.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names, ideally translated into French. Keep medications in original packaging. French customs may inspect medications. An 'ordonnance' (French prescription) format is ideal but English documentation is accepted.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is highly recommended. Healthcare costs follow French pricing which can be expensive for tourists without coverage. Medical evacuation from remote atolls can be very costly. Ensure coverage for water sports and diving if planned.

required: Yellow Fever (only if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
recommended: Typhoid (for extended stays or outer island travel)
vaccinations.notes: No major vaccination concerns for most travelers. There is no malaria in French Polynesia. Dengue fever outbreaks occur periodically — use mosquito repellent. Zika and chikungunya have also been reported.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink in Tahiti and Bora Bora. Water quality on some smaller and more remote atolls may vary — use bottled water when uncertain. Hotels and resorts provide safe drinking water. Bottled water is widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are generally good, following French norms. Fresh fish (poisson cru, the national dish) is safe at established restaurants. Be cautious of ciguatera fish poisoning — locals know which reef fish to avoid. Tropical fruit is abundant and safe. Resort dining meets international standards.
medicalTourismNote: French Polynesia is not a medical tourism destination, though it is a major wellness and honeymoon destination. Spa and wellness treatments at luxury resorts are popular.
sources: French Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé)
metaDescription: French Polynesia health guide for travelers. Emergency numbers, French healthcare system, safe water in Tahiti, pharmacy info, and dengue prevention tips.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier de la Polynésie Française (CHPF)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for all of French Polynesia. Modern facility with emergency, surgical, and specialist departments. French-speaking; limited English. Handles trauma, cardiac, and complex cases.

hospitals.name: Clinique Paofai
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in Papeete. Good general care and some specialties. French-speaking staff.

hospitals.name: Centre Médical de Bora Bora
hospitals.notes: Small medical center on Bora Bora. Handles routine care and minor emergencies. Serious cases transferred to Tahiti by air.

dentalCare.availability: Several dental practices in Papeete and surrounding Tahiti. Very limited on outer islands.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care in Tahiti follows French standards and is of good quality. French-speaking dentists. Costs are higher than mainland France. Outer islands have no dental services.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, private dental clinics in Papeete can handle most urgent issues. CHPF has an oral surgery department for severe cases.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very few English-speaking therapists. Most mental health services are in French.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services follow the French model. CHPF has a psychiatric department. Private psychologists and psychiatrists available in Papeete. Services on outer islands are minimal.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility varies significantly. Luxury resorts on Tahiti and Bora Bora may have good accessibility features. Public infrastructure and outer islands have limited accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: CHPF is a modern hospital with wheelchair access. Smaller medical centers may be less accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Resorts may offer accessible shuttle services. Overwater bungalows are generally not wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact your resort in advance about accessibility needs. Beach access may be difficult. Boat transfers between islands and to overwater bungalows present challenges for wheelchair users.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Some healthcare facilities may still require masks.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at CHPF and some private labs in Papeete.
covidStatus.notes: COVID situation has stabilized. French Polynesia follows metropolitan France's health guidelines.

insuranceClaimProcess: Keep all receipts (feuilles de soins) and medical reports. French-style itemized bills are standard. Facilities may accept credit cards; some require upfront payment. Submit claims with documentation to your insurer. EU EHIC cards are NOT valid in French Polynesia. CFP franc (XPF) is the local currency.

commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs follow French pricing and can be significant. CFP franc (XPF) is the local currency. Credit cards accepted at major facilities. Inter-island medical transfers add substantial cost.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Auckland, New Zealand or metropolitan France
medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation from remote atolls to Tahiti is the primary concern. Air Tahiti operates inter-island flights. For cases beyond CHPF's capacity, evacuation to New Zealand or France is arranged. French military aircraft may assist in emergencies.
